title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 2nd District
area: New Orleans, Jefferson Parish, St. Bernard Parish and the River Parishes of southeast Louisiana.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026. If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map.

summary.text: Troy Carter represents Louisiana's 2nd Congressional District, covering New Orleans, Jefferson, St. Bernard and the River Parishes. A New Orleans native, he held local and state office, including the New Orleans City Council and the Louisiana Senate, before winning a 2021 special election to the U.S. House; he is now in his third term and seeking re-election. He serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the House Homeland Security Committee, is a Deputy Whip for House Democratic leadership, and is 1st Vice Chairman of the Congressional Black Caucus.

background.text: Born in New Orleans in 1963, according to Ballotpedia.

Graduate of Xavier University of Louisiana (BA, political science and business administration) and the University of Holy Cross (MS, business, summa cum laude); he has also received honorary doctorates of humane letters from Xavier University and Southern University of New Orleans.

His public service began as an Executive Assistant to New Orleans Mayor Sidney Barthelemy. Ballotpedia lists his career experience as a business consultant and managing partner of Policy and Planning Partners, LLC.

In 1991, became the first African American elected to represent Louisiana's 102nd District in the Louisiana House of Representatives, where he also served as the youngest-ever floor leader for New Orleans; later became the first African American elected to New Orleans City Council District C.
Sought the 2nd District congressional seat before: he finished fifth in the 2006 all-party general election and sixth in the 2008 Democratic primary, according to Roll Call.

Served as a Louisiana State Senator for the 7th District, including as Senate Minority Leader and as the first African American to represent the district; Roll Call describes him as a state senator since 2015. His official biography says he authored or co-authored hundreds of laws on infrastructure, economic development, women's healthcare, criminal justice reform and reducing homelessness.

Won an April 24, 2021 special election runoff against fellow state Sen. Karen Carter Peterson, 56 percent to 44 percent when the race was called, to succeed Cedric Richmond; Roll Call reported that Carter ran as a centrist and consensus builder.

In the 119th Congress serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee, the Homeland Security Committee and the Democratic Steering and Policy Committee; was selected as a Deputy Whip, elected 1st Vice Chairman of the Congressional Black Caucus, and previously served on the Small Business and Transportation and Infrastructure Committees.

According to his official biography, he is an Adjunct Professor of Political Science at Xavier University, hosts the podcast "What Makes America Tick," and is married to Major General Ana Carter of the U.S. Army, with whom he has two sons, Troy Jr. and Joshua.

priorities.text: Site describes him as authoring or co-authoring laws focused on infrastructure, economic development, women's healthcare, criminal justice reform and reducing homelessness during his time in the Louisiana Legislature.
Describes himself as a steadfast advocate for civil rights, healthcare and environmental justice.

positions.summary: Official biography describes him as an advocate for healthcare and having authored legislation on women's healthcare in the Louisiana Legislature.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the House Homeland Security Committee in the 119th Congress; previously served on the Committees on Small Business and on Transportation and Infrastructure.
Elected 1st Vice Chairman of the Congressional Black Caucus and selected by House Democratic leadership as a Deputy Whip on the House floor.

summary.text: Renada Collins is a banking executive and entrepreneur running for Louisiana's 2nd Congressional District; Ballotpedia lists her as unaffiliated. She describes herself as a business founder, and her campaign emphasizes a livable wage, federal funding for infrastructure, and housing affordability and stability.

background.text: Describes entering the business world in 1999 and launching her own makeup line in 2005; her Ballotpedia profile lists her profession as banking executive.

Describes leading a group of ventures: Big Mouth Media Group (a media platform), Fresh Awakening (focused on spiritual, emotional, physical and economic growth) and the Chicken Scratch Journal Club (which works with authors).
Appeared on the ballot in the October 11, 2025 New Orleans mayoral primary, which Helena Moreno won outright with 54.9 percent.

priorities.text: Says her candidacy prioritizes an economic model favoring residents' well-being over corporate interests, including advocating for a livable wage tied to the true cost of living.
Wants to direct federal infrastructure funding to local needs such as fixing broken water mains and maintaining fire hydrants.
Campaigns on making housing affordable, targeting 80% of Area Median Income, and providing "Voucher Literacy" to help residents use housing benefits.

positions.summary: Campaign message "People Over Profit" calls for a livable wage that reflects the true cost of living.
Campaigns on housing as "a fundamental right" and on making housing affordable at 80% of Area Median Income, with help navigating housing vouchers.

summary.text: Peter Williams is the Republican candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 2nd Congressional District. A tree farmer and former physical education teacher from Lettsworth in Pointe Coupee Parish, he lists agriculture, health, housing, education, transportation, recreation and incarceration as the areas of his platform.

background.text: Graduated from Kaplan High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Southwestern Louisiana (now the University of Louisiana at Lafayette) in 1980.

According to his Ballotpedia survey, he taught physical education in public schools and then worked for Lafayette Parks and Recreation, where he became the first recreation director at the Martin Luther King center.

States that after marrying in 1981 and entering ministry he moved to Pointe Coupee Parish, and that since 1999 he has been a tree farmer and agribusiness conservation specialist growing hardwood seedlings for reforestation; he lives in Lettsworth.
Appeared on the November 5, 2024 ballot for Louisiana's 6th Congressional District, receiving 6,252 votes (2.1 percent); Cleo Fields won outright.
Says he is married to Alfreda Rodney Williams and that they have four grown children and five grandchildren.

summary.text: Lisa Ballay is the Libertarian Party candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 2nd Congressional District. No further biographical information was found in the public record.

Walter Beach is an unaffiliated candidate on the ballot for Louisiana's 2nd Congressional District. A paramedic for more than 37 years, he describes himself as a non-career politician, and his campaign materials include support for election-integrity measures such as the SAVE Act.

background.text: Graduated from Chester High School and earned an associate degree from the University of Louisiana at Lafayette (1991) and a bachelor's degree from Southeastern Louisiana University (2004).
Says he has worked as a paramedic for more than 37 years, alongside firefighters, law enforcement, dispatchers, nurses and doctors; describes himself as "not a career politician."
